subject: Temporary capacity uplift & amortized overrun option
messages:
From: Harper Jansen <harper@horizonai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Riley Thompson <riley.thompson@horizonai.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary quota uplift + amortized overrun option

Hi Tessa —

Hope you’re well. We have a product launch spike the week of May 24 that will push us ~3.5x above our committed throughput for ~72 hours. Procurement asked if we can: (a) get a short-term capacity uplift to avoid throttling during launch, and (b) agree to an amortized overrun charge (so the excess cost is spread across the next 3 invoices) instead of a one-time surge invoice.

Two quick asks: can you tell us the incremental per-token overrun rate for a short window and whether Redwood supports amortizing that charge across invoices? We’d like to present a concrete number to enable sign-off from finance.

Attached is a small preview of expected traffic by route. Happy to jump on a quick call.

—Harper
Head of Platform Operations
HorizonAI
attachments: traffic_preview_May24-26.xlsx (xls)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Harper Jansen <harper@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary quota uplift + amortized overrun option

Hi Harper —

Thanks — we can absolutely support a short window uplift plus an amortized true-up. Two practical paths we recommend depending on how predictable the spike is:

1) Provisional headroom + blended overrun: we reserve provisional capacity for the launch window and any overrun during that window is billed at a blended overrun rate (your committed unit price + 25% surcharge). Overrun dollars are amortized equally over the next 3 monthly invoices. This avoids a single large invoice and smooths cashflow.

2) Temporary tier uplift: move you to the next rate tier for a 30-day window; usage beyond that tier is billed at the higher tier rate (no amortization). More straightforward but less flexible.

Attached is a short draft amendment (draft_amendment_v2.pdf) that encodes option #1 (provisional headroom + 3-month amortization). Key points: 72h guaranteed uplift window, cap the total amortized surcharge at 40% of the uplifted overrun dollars, and invoice timing notes.

If you want the blended numbers now: your committed token rate is $0.0024/token. For a provisional uplift we’d propose an amortized overrun rate equivalent to $0.0030/token (≈+25% blended) with a cap as above. If Horizon prefers a smaller surcharge we can reduce it to +15% but extend amortization to 6 months.

Can you confirm which direction you prefer and whether Procurement needs the amendment as a redlineed PDF or a one-page commercial summary for their approval? Happy to hop on a 20-min call today.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: draft_amendment_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Request: temporary quota uplift + amortized overrun option

Looping in finance/legal considerations. A couple of internal notes:

- Finance prefers cap language expressed as a dollar ceiling (suggest $75k) rather than a percentage to simplify reconciliation.
- Suggest we add a one-time goodwill credit of up to $10k if Horizon sustains >25% higher baseline over 60 days post-launch; that helps procurement sell it.
- Legal will want explicit language on what triggers amortization (we should avoid ambiguous "expected launch" phrasing).

If Tessa’s commercial framing is acceptable to them, I’m fine with the +25%/3-month default. I’ll draft the dollar cap language and propose the credit be conditional on adoption of the 3-month amortization.

—Ben
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Riley Thompson <riley.thompson@horizonai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Harper Jansen <harper@horizonai.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota uplift + amortized overrun option

Thanks — this is helpful context. Horizon prefers option #1 (provisional headroom + amortized true-up). A few clarifications:

- Can you confirm the dollar cap on the amortized surcharge? Procurement asked for a concrete ceiling.
- If we accept the +25%/3-month plan, we will need a one-page commercial summary for our procurement team that lists the uplift window, amortization math, and invoice schedule.

I attached a short usage sample (usage_report_May2027.csv) showing the expected 72h peak. We’d like to proceed but need the cap and the one-pager.

Riley
Program Manager, Launch Ops
HorizonAI
attachments: usage_report_May2027.csv (csv)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Riley Thompson <riley.thompson@redwood.com>, Harper Jansen <harper@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary quota uplift + amortized overrun option

Riley/Harper —

Great — glad you want to proceed with option #1. Final commercial points we’ll include in the one-pager and amendment:

- Guaranteed uplift window: 2027-05-24T00:00:00Z through 2027-05-26T23:59:59Z (72h).
- Amortization: overrun dollars incurred during uplift window amortized equally across the next 3 monthly invoices.
- Amortized surcharge: +25% blended over committed unit price (resulting example rate ≈ $0.0030/token).
- Dollar cap on amortized surcharge: $75,000 total. Any excess overrun beyond that cap will revert to standard overrun billing and is payable on the next invoice.
- One-time conditional credit: up to $10,000 applied on the second invoice if post-launch baseline sustains >25% of pre-launch average for at least 60 days.

Next steps: I’ll have a clean one-page commercial summary for Procurement and a redline-ready amendment for Legal by EOD tomorrow. Ben — can you and Legal stitch the dollar cap and conditional credit language into the attached draft? Karthik — can you confirm routing so this uplift is isolated to the US region and does not impact EU capacity pools?

Harper/Riley — if that looks good, I’ll include the HubSpot deal link and ask our Billing team to schedule invoice amortization.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
